ours-evaluate.short: Night School's evaluation runs, computed for this film
ours-evaluate.citation: media/school/evaluate/facts.json, written by tools/school/fill_evaluate.mjs from system/school/evaluate*.mjs: the attention model retrained at three seeds and scored at eight checkpoints by held-out loss, exact match on one-answer questions, a perfect grammar judge and a cheap word-pair judge, all with bootstrap intervals; judge agreement and order tests; contamination runs with test rows leaked into training.
claims: Step 200: loss 0.873, exact 0.179, perfect judge 0.743, cheap judge 0.973; step 2000: loss 0.673, exact 0.990.
One of 39 checkpoint pairs gives opposite resolved verdicts; 6 pairs loss better with exact match unresolved.
Cheap judge keeps its verdict after a swap on 0.274 of differing pairs; leaking 256 rows 16 times moves loss by 0.0065 on average; 32 rows 250 times by 0.305.
ours-evaluate.does_not_prove: Anything about large models, LLM judges or web-scale contamination; the cheap judge's biases are written into its rule.

zheng2023.short: Zheng and others 2023, Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
zheng2023.citation: Zheng, L., Chiang, W.-L., Sheng, Y., and others (2023). Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena. arXiv:2306.05685; NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks.
zheng2023.read: to be read by the fact-check
claims: LLM judges show position bias; GPT-4 was consistent under swapped order in 65.0 percent of cases.

sainz2023.short: Sainz and others 2023, NLP Evaluation in trouble
sainz2023.citation: Sainz, O., Campos, J. A., Garcia-Ferrero, I., Etxaniz, J., Lopez de Lacalle, O., Agirre, E. (2023). NLP Evaluation in trouble: On the Need to Measure LLM Data Contamination for each Benchmark. Findings of EMNLP 2023. arXiv:2310.18018.
sainz2023.read: to be read by the fact-check
claims: Benchmark test data in the pretraining corpus inflates reported scores; contamination should be measured per benchmark.
